w: George Washington Vanderbilt II built this Chateauesque mansion between 1889 and 1895; at nearly 179,000 square feet of floor space it remains the largest privately owned house in the United States. Still held by Vanderbilt's descendants, it stands as one of the country's most prominent Gilded Age mansions.
s: America's largest private house, still a Vanderbilt's
_facts: Built 1889-1895 for George Washington Vanderbilt II
178,926 sq ft floor space, largest private house in the US
Chateauesque style
Still owned by Vanderbilt's descendants

w: Built in the Arts and Crafts style on the slope of Sunset Mountain, this resort has been visited by various US presidents and sits on the National Register of Historic Places. Its 140 acres now hold 513 guest rooms, ten restaurants, a subterranean spa and an 18-hole golf course.
s: An Arts and Crafts resort that's hosted US presidents
_facts: Arts and Crafts style, on the slope of Sunset Mountain
Visited by various US presidents
On the National Register of Historic Places
140 acres, 513 rooms, an 18-hole golf course

w: Run by the Southern Highland Craft Guild with the National Park Service and the Appalachian Regional Commission, this milepost-382 museum has been the single most popular stop on the Blue Ridge Parkway since opening here in 1980 -- a quarter million visitors a year for Appalachian folk art and craft, free of charge.
s: The Blue Ridge Parkway's single busiest stop
_facts: Museum of Appalachian folk art and craft, milepost 382
Most popular attraction on the Blue Ridge Parkway
About 250,000 visitors a year
Opened at this site in 1980; free admission

w: On downtown Asheville's central square, this museum builds its collection around 20th- and 21st-century American art, with particular depth in Studio Craft and in work tied to Black Mountain College and Cherokee artists -- strands of Western North Carolina's cultural heritage under one accredited roof.
s: Downtown art rooted in Black Mountain College
_facts: Located at 2 South Pack Square, Pack Place
Collection centers on 20th/21st-century American art
Strong Studio Craft, Black Mountain College, and Cherokee holdings
Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums

w: Frederick Law Olmsted floated the idea of an arboretum here in 1898, envisioned as part of the Biltmore Estate he was landscaping nearby. It took until 1986 to become reality, a UNC facility inside the Pisgah National Forest. Its 1950-planted Metasequoia trees are now said to be the tallest in the South.
s: An Olmsted idea, a century in the making
_facts: Idea dates to Frederick Law Olmsted, 1898, tied to Biltmore
Established 1986 as a University of North Carolina facility
434 acres within the Pisgah National Forest
Metasequoias planted 1950, reputedly the tallest in the South
